I really hate how the light tunnel is treated as "the LSD scene" instead of a masterful example of abstract expressionism in film. Sure, drugs were involved, but all art takes on influences from its contemporary culture. It was the late sixties, and LSD was influencing all forms of art. So was... space travel! But nobody complains when you make a movie about space exploration. Why? Psychedelic drugs are arguably safe enough that most people can enjoy them. More people have been to the moon and back without a spaceship than with one. So what is the greater influence on our culture? LSD or the moon landing?

I've never partaken in LSD and don't really plan to unless it is legalized, regulated, and pure, but i still think that scene is amazing. Sometimes I watch it without watching the rest of the movie. It's that good. It's remarkably abstract, but it does a remarkable job at getting it's audience to feel as if they were traveling through a wormhole. That's great abstract expressionism. It's also a great example of an artist working with subject matters that go beyond his technical limits. Kubrick didn't have CGI. How was he supposed to realistically depict traveling through a wormhole? He couldn't. So, he did what any artist would do. Instead of doing a poor job with a realistic depiction, he did a magnificent job using a figurative expression of what going through a "light tunnel" might feel like.
